prompt:
Precise P1 crayon style adjustment. IMAGE 1 is the original richly colored P1 walking dog and is the EDIT TARGET. IMAGE 2 is a child's drawing used only for irregular crayon pressure and imperfect pigment coverage. Do not use or reproduce the previous very sparsely colored P1 experiment: the user rejected that as too empty.
Preserve image 1's same walking pose, underlying four-leg anatomy, whole-body composition, low feathered gray tail, short floppy ears, gray/white marking layout, white forehead blaze into muzzle/beard, white bib and paws, and small ROUND dark dot eyes. Keep the same character and palette, no rainbow outline colors, no new white patches. Square canvas, warm paper background.
FUR CHANGE IS SMALL: retain the original clearly GRAY ears, outer face, back, flank and tail as continuous recognizably filled regions. Reduce their crayon filling density ONLY SLIGHTLY, roughly retain 85–90% of the original visual density. Add just a little more paper grain and small irregular uncolored gaps within the gray fill; do not erase large areas, do not replace full gray regions with a few stripes, do not make the torso mostly paper-white. Keep white fur areas readable as white rather than changing the markings. Retain original simple fur silhouette, lightly hand-wobbled lines but no drastic simplification or anatomy change.
CONCENTRATE CHILDLIKE IMPERFECTION IN EYES / NOSE / TONGUE:
- Keep both eyes SMALL ROUND DOTS with exactly the existing approximate size, spacing and positions. Dark charcoal-brown pigment is still substantially filled, but edges are slightly uneven, pressure varies and a tiny amount of natural paper tooth shows. No glossy highlights, white catchlight dots, white sclera, perfect vector disks, eyelashes, enlarged anime eyes or elongated ovals. Tiny pigment gaps must read as dry crayon paper texture, never sparkling eyes. Subtle natural difference in the two marks is enough.
- Nose remains the same dark rounded triangular shape and location; give it a slightly lopsided hand-drawn boundary and a few tiny unfilled paper speckles rather than a mechanically solid or shiny nose. Keep it dark and clearly readable.
- Tongue remains the same small pink shape and mouth position. Pink crayon coverage is irregular with modest little paper gaps and a slight mismatch between outline and fill. Avoid a glossy central white streak or reflective highlight. This is incomplete child's coloring, NOT a change of tongue color, anatomy or expression.
The total dog should still look as fully gray-and-white as image 1 at first glance. The face marks should gain modest handmade irregularity and dry crayon coverage, not glossy polish. No dense new detail, additional objects, labels, UI, scenery, frames or annotations.
user_feedback: Previous sparse filling was too little. Reduce fur density only slightly; apply childlike imperfect marks/filling to eyes, nose and tongue.
coverage_measurement: not_performed; numeric density in prompt is a qualitative target, not measured output
